# 4 Ezra Chapter 3 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Latin Vulgate (Codex Sangermanensis) | **Section:** Core apocalypse — First dialogue

---

**3:1** In the thirtieth year after the destruction of the city, I, Salathiel — also known as Ezra — was in Babylon. I lay upon my bed in distress, and troubled thoughts welled up in my heart,

**3:2** for I saw the desolation of Zion and the wealth of those who dwell in Babylon.

**3:3** My spirit was greatly agitated, and I began to speak anxious words before the Most High,

**3:4** saying: O LORD, you who dwell in eternity, whose eyes are lifted up and whose upper chambers are in the air,

**3:5** whose throne is beyond measure and whose glory is beyond comprehension, before whom the host of angels stands trembling,

**3:6** whose service is transformed into wind and fire, whose word is true and utterances steadfast, whose ordinance is mighty and commandment fearsome,

**3:7** whose glance dries up the depths, whose anger makes the mountains melt, and whose truth endures forever:

**3:8** Hear, O LORD, the prayer of your servant, and give ear to the petition of your creature; attend to my words.

**3:9** For as long as I live I will speak, and as long as I have understanding I will respond.

**3:10** Do not regard the sins of your people, but those who served you in truth.

**3:11** Do not take into account the endeavors of those who practice wickedness, but those who kept your covenants amid affliction.

**3:12** Do not call to mind those who walked in wicked ways before you, but remember those who willingly acknowledged their fear of you.

**3:13** Let it not be your will to destroy those who lived like cattle; but look upon those who have clearly taught your law.

**3:14** Do not be angry with those deemed worse than animals, but love those who have always placed their trust in your righteousness and glory.

**3:15** For we and our fathers have passed our lives in ways that bring death; but you, on account of us sinners, are called merciful.

**3:16** For if you desire to have mercy upon us who have no works of righteousness, then you shall be called the Merciful One.

**3:17** For the righteous, who have stored up many works with you, shall receive their reward in consequence of their own works.

**3:18** But what is man, that you are angry with him? What is a mortal race, that you should be bitter toward it?

**3:19** For in truth there is no one born who has not sinned, and among all who have lived there is none who did no wrong.

**3:20** For in this, O LORD, your righteousness and goodness shall be declared, when you are merciful to those who have no treasury of good works.

**3:21** Then I answered and said: You spoke in the beginning, when you formed the earth alone and commanded the dust,

**3:22** and Adam obeyed you. You gave him a living soul; he was your workmanship, the work of your hands. You breathed into him the breath of life, and he was made alive before you.

**3:23** And you led him into paradise, which your right hand had planted before the earth appeared.

**3:24** And you laid upon him one commandment of yours; but he transgressed it, and immediately you appointed death for him and for his generations; and from him were born nations and peoples and all tribes, whose multitude cannot be numbered.

**3:25** And every nation walked according to its own will, behaved wickedly before you and despised your commandments, and you did not restrain them.

**3:26** But in due time you brought the flood upon the inhabitants of the world and destroyed them.

**3:27** And the same fate came upon all — as death came upon Adam, so the flood came upon them.

**3:28** But you preserved one of them — Noah with his household — all the righteous ones who descended from him.

**3:29** And when the inhabitants of the earth began to multiply, and children, nations, and many peoples increased, they began again to practice ungodliness, worse than before.

**3:30** And while they were sinning before you, you chose out one of them, whose name was Abraham;

**3:31** and you loved him, and to him alone you revealed the end of the times, in secret, by night.

**3:32** And you made with him an everlasting covenant and promised him that you would never forsake his descendants.

**3:33** And you gave him Isaac, and to Isaac you gave Jacob and Esau. Jacob you set apart for yourself, but Esau you rejected; and Jacob became a great multitude.

**3:34** And when you led his descendants out of Egypt, you brought them to Mount Sinai.

**3:35** You bowed down the heavens, shook the earth, moved the world, made the depths tremble, and troubled the whole creation.

**3:36** And your glory passed through four gates of fire and earthquake and wind and ice, to give the law to the seed of Jacob and the commandment to the generation of Israel.
